svg.title: Defender Emulated Circuit
svg.desc: Block schematic of the Williams Defender (1981) hardware as simulated in src/defender/index.html: the MC6809E main CPU with its RAM, ROM banks, CMOS, colour palette, two MC6821 PIAs and video timing, and the MC6808 sound board with its PIA and MC1408 DAC.
svg.text: Williams Electronics, 1981 — the chips and signals simulated in src/defender/index.html (hardware reference: MAME williams driver)
Source: mwenge/defender @ e740063 (Eugene Jarvis, Sam Dicker)
Assembled in the browser: 6809, 6309 and 6800 assemblers
→ 11 game ROMs + defend.snd, each cut, patched and
ROM; a write selects the bank
The game writes a sound number to ROM PIA
port B; PB6 and PB7 read high on the sound
Any other value raises CB1 → IRQ, and the
6808 reads the command from its port B.
It plays by writing samples to port A,
260 scan lines, each cut into 16 slices: the 6809 runs
4 cycles and the 6808 about 3.58 cycles per slice.
The timing chain toggles CA1/CB1 of the ROM PIA, and
lines 7–246 are drawn from RAM through the palette.
